item.research_question: Can epitaxial strain selectively stabilize specific magneto-electronic states and control spin orientation in chemically complex high entropy oxides (HEOs) despite local chemical heterogeneity?
item.material_system: (Co0.2Cr0.2Fe0.2Mn0.2Ni0.2)3O4 spinel high entropy oxide (HEO) thin films
item.processing_route: Laser pulsed deposition (PLD) at 690 °C in 0.03 mbar oxygen pressure using a KrF excimer laser (248 nm, 5 Hz, 1.55 J cm−2) on MgO (001), STO (001), and MAO (001) substrates to induce tensile, relaxed, and compressive strain states respectively; films cooled at 20 °C min−1
item.test_conditions: Magnetic measurements at 5 K and 300 K using SQUID magnetometry; Magnetic Force Microscopy (MFM) at room temperature; Structural characterization via XRD, XRR, RSM, AFM, and TEM
key_findings: The film on MgO exhibits tensile strain (ε = +0.97%) resulting in an in-plane easy axis and a hard out-of-plane (OOP) axis with linear M-H curves up to 70 kOe.
The film on MAO exhibits compressive strain (ε = −3.19%) resulting in perpendicular magnetic anisotropy (PMA) with an OOP easy axis and a square-like hysteresis loop.
The film on STO is relaxed (ε ≈ −0.4%) and displays isotropic magnetization behavior similar to bulk HEO.
A unique coexistence of fully coherent spinel and rocksalt HEO phases is observed in all films with no detectable chemical segregation.
MFM reveals a maze-like domain structure in compressively strained films, indicative of OOP magnetic anisotropy.
Tensile strain increases the hardness of the OOP axis significantly, while compressive strain creates an easy OOP magnetization.
The magnetic transition temperature remains well above room temperature across all strain states.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute the strain-driven spin reorientation to magneto-elastic coupling where spin-orbit interaction (L orb × S) couples the partially quenched orbital moments of Co and Ni ions to the crystal field; compressive strain aligns the easy axis OOP, while tensile strain aligns it in-plane.
item.limitations: The exact ratio of rocksalt-HEO to spinel-HEO phases is difficult to quantify; the specific reason for the universal formation of dual phases in thin films versus bulk remains an open question; the precise ion distribution and charge states in the epitaxial films cannot be readily obtained due to chemical complexity.
item.future_work: Further investigation is needed to understand the origin and mechanism related to the rocksalt-HEO phase formation in (Co0.2Cr0.2Fe0.2Mn0.2Ni0.2)3O4 epitaxial thin films and the thermodynamics of HEOs.
quotes: Epitaxial strain can selectively stabilize specific magnetoelectronic states, despite the extreme local chemical and bonding heterogeneity of HEOs.
Compressive straining results in an easy OOP magnetization and a maze-like magnetic domain structure, indicating the perpendicular magnetic anisotropy.

The formation or dissociation of the spinel-HEO phase into rocksalt-HEO and spinel-HEO with close lattice constants and chemical compositions appears to be a universal phenomenon that is not otherwise observed in the bulk.
